fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK/PHB display against background clutter is a real, documented driver-comprehension hazard with direct crash potential for crossing pedestrians, and it remains addressable at Final Design stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time visual elements at Speedway/Rook) is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-001 traceable to the FHWA case-study issue table, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed purely as a safety_concern rather than a compliance question under FHWA RSA practice, uses US HAWK/PHB terminology consistently, and makes no improper normative-basis assertion.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Retroreflective bordering of the beacon head is a specific, established, buildable conspicuity countermeasure for the named intersection, though it could optionally extend to auditing adjacent light/sign clutter sources.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the exposed vulnerable users—are explicitly identified in road_users and scenario, with the driver-conspicuity-to-pedestrian-risk linkage clearly articulated as inference.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing at the corridor's highest pedestrian-collision-frequency HAWK sites is a genuine, scheme-relevant safety issue for slower walkers caught in the crosswalk at phase change.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim ('may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') is backed by a verbatim quote from cited EV-US-016 recorded for these exact sites per the confidence basis.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA final-design semantics with no compliance question conflated; HAWK/pedestrian clearance concepts used appropriately.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: names the action (reprogramme clearance intervals), all six sites, and the method (reduced assumed walking speed), and is viable at final-design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Vulnerable road users are the explicit focus—elderly pedestrians named in road_users, scenario, and underlying recorded issue—with impacts fully considered.
